_comment: Macro engine for the Pounds On-Ramp. Targets stated by Dr. Cavo. Every null marked TODO(sharepoint) must be filled from practice source material before a patient build is allowed.

calories.answeredBy: Cavo 2026-08-26: protein takes priority. Going over 1200 to hit protein is allowed.
calories.TODO(cavo): How far over 1200 is acceptable before it stops being a 1200 calorie plan? Build warns above 1250 but will not fail while protein is in range.

protein.answeredBy: Cavo 2026-08-26: '90-110g is the range' + 'Protein takes the priority.'
protein.revisedBy: Cavo, relayed by Tyler 2026-08-27: days CAN run over on protein. So 110 is a soft upper reference, not a ceiling. 90g is the enforced floor and there is no maximum.
protein.PROVENANCE: Relayed verbally through Tyler, NOT in writing from Cavo. Confirm in the sign-off email before the patient copy ships.

fat.answeredBy: Tyler 2026-08-27: track fat, carbs and protein.
fat.note: Tracked and displayed on every day and in the patient copy. No band is set, so a day cannot fail on fat - but a day with UNKNOWN fat is now incomplete rather than acceptable.
fat.TODO: Days 1-5 come from the 1,150 menu, which states calories, carb and protein only. Their fat is unknown and will NOT be derived. The RD needs to supply it, or those days stay flagged.

_wheyNote: Cavo 2026-08-27: 'The protein supplement counts towards the 1200 cal diet.' So the whey's protein and calories come OUT of the daily budget, and food must hit the bands with the whey included, not on top of it.

_tracksNote: Cavo 2026-08-26: standard first. Variants deferred, not cancelled.

claimsRequiringSubstantiation.note: Creatine for muscle preservation is defensible. Needs a source in _source/ before it appears in patient copy.
Blood-sugar language on a supplement recommended to every patient is the highest-risk sentence in the document. Needs Cavo substantiation or it does not ship in patient copy.

compliance.signoffNote: Tyler 2026-08-27: any of the practice's dietitians may review the plans they put together, not only Pam or Alisha. The staff copy records WHO signed, not which name was expected.

clinicalFlags.issue: KetoCitra is marketed as a medical food for chronic kidney conditions. Its mechanism is a potassium and calcium citrate blend. Cavo has asked for it to be recommended to EVERY new patient as muscle preserving and sugar stabilizing.
clinicalFlags.why: The product itself claims neither muscle preservation nor blood-sugar stabilisation. A daily potassium load recommended blanket-wide is a prescribing decision, not a content decision - it interacts with renal function and with ACE inhibitors, ARBs and potassium-sparing diuretics.
clinicalFlags.action: Cavo confirms in writing, with a dose, before this appears in any patient copy.

clinicalFlags.issue: The gummies are literally named 'Blood Sugar Support' and the copy claims GLP-1 production and glycemic blunting, each carrying the FDA structure/function asterisk.
clinicalFlags.why: This substantiates Cavo's 'sugar stabilizing' phrase as a manufacturer claim, but a manufacturer claim carried into a physician's patient protocol reads as a clinical endorsement.
clinicalFlags.action: Keep the asterisked disclaimer wording, or drop the phrase from patient copy.

planDecisions.decision: The whey occupies one numbered meal slot rather than sitting alongside the food.
planDecisions.why: Cavo: the protein supplement counts towards the 1200. If it were additional to four full meals the day would overshoot. Their own patient planner runs MEAL #1 to #6, so the shake takes a slot.
planDecisions.status: PROPOSED - needs a nod from Cavo or the reviewing RD, not a label lookup.

trackNotes.dairy-free: PARTIAL SOURCE. '1200-1300 cals low dairy 110 g p' exists but is LOW dairy, not dairy-free - it still contains feta, mozzarella and Laughing Cow, so it is not safe for an allergy. It also states no carbohydrate. Substitute protein IS named in practice material: OWYN dairy-free shake, Kite Hill yogurt, vegan protein powder.
trackNotes.vegan: COMPONENTS ONLY. Six branded vegan entrees carry full macros; no assembled menu at 1,200 kcal / 90 g protein exists. Every plant-based menu in the dump states meal names without macros.

approvedSources._status: PROPOSED - NOT YET APPROVED BY CAVO. No food has been added under this yet.
approvedSources._why: The vegan track cannot be built from practice material: the best day assemblable is 4 g protein against a 90 g floor. Filling it needs food data from outside _source/, which is a deliberate departure from 'practice material only' and therefore Cavo's call, not the builder's.
approvedSources._rule: Any food added from outside _source/ MUST carry sourceType and a citation (FDC id, or manufacturer + label URL). The build rejects a food with neither a _source/ file nor an approved citation.

candidates.name: USDA FoodData Central
candidates.covers: Generic whole foods: tofu, tempeh, lentils, seitan, legumes, grains.
candidates.why: US government reference data. Authoritative, free, per-100g and per-serving.
candidates.caveat: Needs a free API key from api.data.gov. Not yet obtained.

candidates.name: Manufacturer nutrition facts panel
candidates.covers: Branded products the practice already recommends: OWYN, Kite Hill, RxSugar, Sola, Catalina Crunch.
candidates.why: Already used once for Naked Whey - the panel was read off the manufacturer site and saved into _source/. Same method, same traceability.
candidates.caveat: Panel must be saved as an image alongside the entry, not just cited.

rejected.name: Recipe sites, blogs, MyFitnessPal user entries, AI estimates
rejected.why: Crowd-entered or generated. No provenance. Not defensible in a patient document.

delivery.primary: printed, or handed over as a meal PDF
delivery.implication: Print fidelity is the priority over screen. Landscape weekly grid, one week per page, collapsed detail expanded before printing, no colour dependence.
